name: Slowdive
label: Creation Records
lede: Five Reading teenagers signed to Creation, got told by the British music press that they were finished, got dropped a week after their third album, and came back twenty years later to bigger crowds than they'd ever had.

eras.title: Friends since they were six
eras.text: Neil Halstead and Rachel Goswell had known each other since they were six and had already been through one indie-pop band together in Reading. Slowdive was the second try, and within about a year it had a deal with Alan McGee's Creation Records and an average age of 19.

years.h: The Pumpkin Fairies end and Slowdive starts in Reading
years.p: Halstead and Goswell keep drummer [[Adrian Sell|6ac7e8df-f501-4a11-b84c-808dcb77f0fe]] from the old band and add [[Nick Chaplin|4eac8629-0b4d-4793-be60-69ddd592afdc]] on bass. The name comes out of a dream Chaplin had.
years.xp: The Pumpkin Fairies, with bassist Mike Cottle, ran from 1988 into 1989. The new band's name came from Chaplin's dream plus a talk with Goswell about a Siouxsie and the Banshees single. Goswell has said she "was outvoted for the choice of the name in the end."

years.h: Christian Savill offers to wear a dress to get the gig
years.p: The band's ad asked for a female guitarist. [[Christian Savill|e9b893d4-c2b4-40ec-b485-d7605f838d5a]] answered it anyway and, as Wikipedia tells it, offered to wear a dress.

years.h: Creation signs a band whose average age is 19
years.p: A demo and a show at Reading's After Dark Club with Five Thirty get the band noticed, and Alan McGee's Creation Records signs them. Drummer Adrian Sell leaves after about six months for university.
years.xp: "That was exciting for us to sign with Creation. It was the best label in the UK at the time," Goswell told Vice. The label was home to [[My Bloody Valentine|8ca01f46-53ac-4af2-8516-55a909c0905e]], [[Ride|3f575ecd-627d-4f08-a89f-abd46d469c7e]] and [[Primal Scream|55704c38-224f-4b75-b29f-d43653f8bc9a]].

years.h: The Slowdive EP is Melody Maker's Single of the Week
years.p: The first Creation release. NME's Simon Williams wrote that the band had "banished the barrier restricting creativity."

eras.title: The scene that celebrates itself
eras.text: By mid-1991 the papers had a name for Slowdive, Ride, Lush and the rest: shoegazing. The same papers turned on it within months, and Slowdive took more of the kicking than most. Then Alan McGee heard the second album's first draft.

years.h: Simon Scott leaves the Charlottes and takes the drum stool
years.p: Neil Carter drums on the Morningrise EP but is gone before it comes out in February. [[Simon Scott|67e98cbd-a16c-498e-b556-0e8ca30a1352]], whose band the Charlottes had just split, comes in.

years.h: "Catch the Breeze" goes to No. 1 on the UK Indie Chart
years.p: The Holding Our Breath EP reaches No. 52 on the main chart. Around now the press starts calling it shoegazing.

years.h: Just for a Day makes the indie top 10 and the critics groan
years.p: NME liked the debut album. Melody Maker's Paul Lester called it a "major fucking letdown," and most of the press followed his lead.
years.xp:
The backlash against shoegaze had begun, and Slowdive were an easy target: young, quiet on stage, and signed to the label of the moment. Peter Buckley's account sums up the reception: "dismissed as dreary and lacking in ideas."

Scott said later the band couldn't work out the venom: "We couldn't understand why people were so outraged by our sound."

q: We will always hate Slowdive more than Hitler.
years.h: Richey Edwards picks Slowdive as the band to hate
years.p: Manic Street Preachers guitarist Richey Edwards put it in print in 1991, a year when the papers were turning on shoegaze.

years.h: SBK stencils Slowdive's name across New York
years.p: The band's American label spray-stencils the name outside MTV and radio stations. It also lands on a statue commemorating the end of slavery. The label also pushes the US release back three months.

years.h: First American trip, opening for Blur
years.p: Slowdive make their first US visit on a tour with [[Blur|ba853904-ae25-4ebb-89d6-c44cfbd71bd2]], after a European run in February. Blue Day collects the early EPs for the shops.

years.cap: Rachel Goswell on stage with Slowdive, 1992
years.h: Alan McGee hears 40 new songs: "They're all shit"
years.p: McGee rejects the first round for the second album. Halstead, just broken up with Goswell, rents a cottage in rural Wales for two weeks and comes back with "Dagger" and "40 Days."
years.xp:
The rejected batch leaned on Joy Division and David Bowie. While Halstead was away, the others killed time in Weston-super-Mare recording what Wikipedia calls "joke songs."

The breakup with Goswell sits underneath the whole record that followed. Both stayed in the band.

years.h: Brian Eno takes the clock off the studio wall
years.p: The band wrote to [[Brian Eno|ff95eb47-41c4-4f7f-a104-cdc30f02e872]] asking him to produce. He wouldn't produce, but he came in to play, and two songs came out of it: "Sing" and "Here She Comes."
years.xp: Halstead called the session "one of the most surreal stoned experiences of my life." Eno's instruction, per Wikipedia: "I don't care what you are going to play, just play something."

eras.title: Career suicide, as reviewed
eras.text: Souvlaki is now on every list of the best shoegaze records. In 1993 it peaked at No. 51, and the American label left it on the shelf for eight months. Two years later Halstead walked away from guitars altogether, and Creation walked away from Slowdive.

years.h: Souvlaki, named after a Jerky Boys prank call
years.p: The second album opens with "Alison" and peaks at No. 51. Melody Maker's Dave Simpson led the pile-on.
years.xp:
Simpson's review: "I would rather drown choking in a bath full of porridge than ever listen to it again." The same paper had called the early EPs "impossible, immaculate and serene." NME's verdict was "pretty, but unfulfilled."

The title came from a crude skit by the American comedy duo the Jerky Boys. Pitchfork later ranked the record among the best shoegaze albums ever made.

years.h: SBK sits on Souvlaki, so Slowdive tour Europe with Cranes
years.p: A US tour with Catherine Wheel was planned. The American label held the album back eight months instead, and the band went round Europe with the dream-pop band Cranes.

years.h: Simon Scott quits over the gap between records
years.p: Scott leaves, unhappy with how long the band waited between releases. [[Ian McCutcheon|1d54d158-0f51-4247-a674-e8ea24c6dd03]] takes over on drums.

years.h: Post 50 flyers, get a free Souvlaki
years.p: SBK's US campaign asked fans to put up 50 flyers and send photos as proof, in exchange for the album. Halfway through the tour, the label pulled its money.
years.xp: AllMusic's Andy Kellman called it "one of the laziest" campaigns ever. With SBK's funding gone mid-tour, the band paid for the rest of the dates by selling live tapes and tour programmes that mocked tour programmes.

years.h: Halstead trades the guitar wall for Pygmalion
years.p: After hearing Aphex Twin's Selected Ambient Works 85–92, Halstead wrote nearly the whole third album alone: sparse, looped, mostly ambient. NME's John Harris called it "career suicide."
years.xp:
Q's Andrew Collins was on side: it "basks splendidly in its own sod-you resonant shapelessness." Melody Maker called it "an insipid attempt at prettiness."

By 2018 Pitchfork was calling it a "post-rock masterpiece," and bands like [[Low|42faad37-8aaa-42e4-a300-5a7dae79ed24]] and Deafheaven had said as much.

years.src: Under the Radar · Vice · Wikipedia: Slowdive
years.h: Creation drops Slowdive a week after Pygmalion comes out
years.p: Savill and Chaplin decide they're done too. "It got terrible reviews, and we all felt, 'Well, fuck it,'" Halstead told Under the Radar.
years.xp:
Goswell felt the label had moved on well before: "It didn't feel like there was much interest within the label," she said of Souvlaki, with Creation's attention on [[Primal Scream|55704c38-224f-4b75-b29f-d43653f8bc9a]] and the Britpop bands.

Halstead doesn't mourn it: "I think it ended at the right time, and I don't regret that."

years.h: Halstead, Goswell and McCutcheon become Mojave 3 on 4AD
years.p: A country-leaning record under a new name. Vice called the debut, Ask Me Tomorrow, "essentially Slowdive unplugged." [[Mojave 3|abf74786-2f3e-47e0-ae68-69a55c13909a]] made four more albums before going quiet in 2008.
years.xp: The others kept going too. Scott formed Televise and later joined Lowgold. Savill started Monster Movie. Halstead and Goswell both made solo albums for 4AD, and Goswell later joined the supergroup Minor Victories.

eras.title: Bigger than the first time
eras.text: In 2004 The Independent called Slowdive a "long-forgotten indie band." Ten years later a festival in Barcelona made them an offer, and the band found a crowd that hadn't been born when Souvlaki came out.

years.cap: Slowdive at NOS Primavera Sound, Porto, June 2014
years.src: Vice · Under the Radar · Wikipedia: Slowdive
years.h: Primavera Sound books Slowdive, and the plan is one show
years.p: The festival's was the first official reunion offer the band had ever had, Halstead said. Simon Scott came back on drums; Ian McCutcheon did not.
years.xp:
Halstead had played a solo show in London in late 2013, and the Primavera offer sealed it, per Vice. One show became a summer of festivals and a 20-date North American tour that October and November.

The band found they were "more famous and recognisable than ever before," with bigger crowds than in the 1990s.

years.cap: Slowdive at the Fox Theater, Oakland, October 2017
years.h: "Star Roving" is the first new Slowdive song in 22 years
years.p: It comes out on Dead Oceans, the band's new label.

years.h: Slowdive, recorded in five studios from Exeter to Cornwall
years.p: The comeback album reaches No. 16 in the UK and gets 8.6 from Pitchfork. Exclaim! called it the album fans had been "dreaming about for the last 22 years."

eras.title: Modular synths and a first Glastonbury
eras.text: The fifth album started as Halstead's solo electronic project and turned into the band's biggest record, made through a stretch when two members lost parents.

years.h: Halstead's synth demos become a Slowdive album
years.p: Halstead had written on modular synthesizers in 2019 for a solo project. Sessions planned for April 2020 were cancelled by COVID-19 and began that September.
years.xp: During the making of the record, Goswell lost her mother and Scott lost his father. Goswell has spoken publicly about her drinking afterwards and about getting sober, as Wikipedia notes.

years.src: Wikipedia: Slowdive · Wikipedia: Everything Is Alive
years.h: Slowdive play Glastonbury for the first time
years.p: Thirty-four years in, the same month "Kisses" comes out as the lead single. Halstead had worried it was "too pop."

years.src: Wikipedia: Everything Is Alive · Wikipedia: Slowdive
years.h: Everything Is Alive is Slowdive's first top-10 album anywhere
years.p: No. 6 in the UK, and top 10 in Belgium, Germany, the Netherlands and New Zealand. Halstead flew to Los Angeles to mix it with Shawn Everett.
